chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yusuf ibn Imran ibn Maysam, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Adam (peace be upon him): 'I shall summarize the speech for you in four sentences.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, and what are they?' He (Mighty and Majestic) said: 'One for Me, and one for you, and one regarding what is between Me and you, and one regarding what is between you and the people.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, explain them to me so that I may know them.' He (Mighty and Majestic) said: 'As for that which is for Me, worship Me and do not associate anything with Me; and as for that which is for you, I shall recompense you for your deeds with what you will be most in need of; and as for that which is between Me and you, upon you is supplication and upon Me is the response; and as for that which is between you and the people, be pleased for the people with what you are pleased with for yourself, and dislike for them what you dislike for yourself.'

key_terms.لَا تُشْرِكُ بِي: Do not associate partners with Me (monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What are the four key aspects of faith and life revealed to Adam (AS) in this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith as a comprehensive framework for Islamic ethics, categorizing the believer's existence into vertical (God-ward) and horizontal (human-ward) dimensions. It uniquely links the metaphysical concept of *Tawhid* with the practical social ethic of *Rida* (contentment/reciprocity), establishing that true monotheism manifests in just treatment of others. This structure reflects the Shia emphasis on the inseparability of creed (*Aqidah*) and conduct (*Amal*), where divine promise (*al-Wa'd*) is contingent upon human supplication and social equity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad in Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Yunus Bin Imran Bin Maysam, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto Adam<sup>as</sup>: “I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Gather the Speech for you in four Sentences”. He<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! And what are these?’ He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: “One for Me<sup>azwj</sup>, and one for You<sup>as</sup>, and one regarding what is between Me<sup>azwj</sup> and you<sup>as</sup>, and one regarding what is between you<sup>as</sup> and the people”.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! Explain these to me<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> until I<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> know these’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Said: “As for that which is for Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, so worship Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, nor associating anything with Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>; and as for that which is for you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, so I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> shall Recompense you for your<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> deeds with what would you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> would happen to be the most needy to; and as for that which is between Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> and you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, so upon you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> is the supplication and upon Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is the Answering; and as for that which is between you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> and the people, so you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> should be pleased with the people what you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> would be pleased with yourself<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, and dislike for them what you<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> would dislike for yourself<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Yusuf ibn ‘Imran ibn Maytham from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, sent a revelation to Adam that said, ‘I will gather together all words for you in four words.’ He asked, ‘O Lord, what are they?’ He said, ‘One is for Me, one for you, one between Me and you and one between you and other people.’

He then said, ‘O Lord, explain them to me so I can learn.’ He said, ‘The one for Me is to worship Me and do not consider anything as My partner. The one for you is that I will reward you for your deed with something that you need most. The one between Me and you is that you pray and I will accept and answer your prayers. The one between you and people is that you must like for people what you like for yourself and dislike for people what you dislike to happen to you.’”
